question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we express $y$ as the composite function

$$
y=\log_{9}(u),\quad u=\sqrt{7 x}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}=\frac{1}{u\ln(9)},\quad \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=\frac{7}{2\sqrt{7 x}}.
$$

We now apply the chain rule, and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} &=\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}u}\cdot \frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}\\ &=\frac{1}{u\ln(9)}\cdot (\frac{7}{2\sqrt{7 x}})\\ &=\frac{1}{(\sqrt{7 x})\ln(9)}\cdot (\frac{7}{2\sqrt{7 x}})\\ &=\frac{7}{2(7 x)\ln(9)}\\ &=\frac{\cancel{7}}{2\cdot \cancel{7}x\ln(9)}\\ &=\frac{1}{2 x \ln{(9 )}}.\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Differentiating a General Logarithm Function Using the Chain Rule

checks.purpose: Isolated logarithm identity on already simplified radical derivative
